findings.location: Page level: the header nav (id nav) and footer (id footer) are the only navigation mechanisms present anywhere in the document.
findings.evidence:
Plan a tripAccessibility
and
Privacy policyTerms of service
; no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere else in the document.
findings.violation: The page provides exactly one navigation mechanism, the primary nav menu with 2 links; no site search, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail exists anywhere in the document, and nothing in the page marks it as one step in a linear process, so the two independent mechanism minimum is not met.
findings.fix: Add a second independent way to reach this page, such as a site search form, a sitemap link, or a breadcrumb trail reflecting the page's place in the site, distinct from the primary nav menu.

findings.location: Fare adjustments section, form, the promo input (id promo) and its adjacent error text (id s3-form-promo-error).
findings.evidence: is immediately followed by Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.; the input carries no aria-describedby, aria-labelledby, or any other attribute referencing the error span's id.
findings.violation: The promo input is marked aria-invalid="true" but has no aria-describedby or other programmatic reference pointing at the adjacent error text span, so the error description is not programmatically associated with the field it describes; a screen reader user tabbing to the field is told it is invalid but not told why without additional exploration.
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" to the promo input so assistive technology announces the error text when the field receives focus.
